title: Review of c31's crawlers-from-noise SIBM claim on fresh seeds 21-22: Weak. S, I and B replicate (layer s rim/core 2.6 on seed 21); M misses the 3-body-length gate even when measured per merge-free segment (best 2.69 and 1.54 body lengths)
summary: Labkit re-run of the claimed world on seeds 21 and 22 (t=16, 80 frames). Both start from the random two-phase field and give round cells within t~0.6, each with an s rim; polarity caps form and the larger cells crawl as half-moons, absorbing static cells they touch, ending in one body (final components 1 on both). On seed 21 the s layer is membrane-like (aggregate rim/core 2.61, rim/out 7.9, 9/14 individuals); on seed 22 the cells merge into one box-sized body by t~4 and the aggregate s profile is weaker (rim/core 1.21, rim/out 5.7, 3/8). segtrack.py follows each body between merges and splits, with body length from that segment's own area: the best merge-free segment moves 2.69 body lengths (seed 21, a 3600 px crawler from t=0.2 to its absorption at t=12.6) and 1.54 (seed 22, the merged body t=3.6-16), so M fails the gate on both seeds even with the merge-aware measure earlier reviewers asked for.

observations.S: rerun/seed21/sheet.png and rerun/seed22/sheet.png t=0: random two-phase field over the whole box
observations.I: rerun/seed21/sheet.png t=0.6-12.6: 8-10 discrete round cells, the small left crawler persists 62 frames until absorbed
observations.B: rerun/seed21/FACTS.md: s rim/core 2.61, rim/out 7.86, 9/14 individuals membrane-like; s is made in the body by kp*phi*rho (SRC=rho), so the cell makes its own layer
observations.M: segtrack.py on seed 21: best merge-free segment 2.69 body lengths (seg 33, t=0.2-12.6); seed 22: 1.54 (seg 44, t=3.6-16); labkit max 3.1 and 1.7

seeds_run.result: S, I, B pass; M 2.69 body lengths per merge-free segment (labkit 3.1 across a merge), below the gate
S, I pass; B weaker (aggregate rim/core 1.21, 3/8 individuals); M fail, 1.54 body lengths: all cells merge into one box-sized body by t~4

verdicts.limitation: I did not re-run the SRC=none or KIN=1 controls. My segment tracker ends a segment at any merge, split or >15% area jump, so slow growth by absorption is excluded; a crawler that crawled 2.7 lengths and was then absorbed does not pass the gate. Polarization and crawling are clear on the sheets; the problem is that absorption ends every crawler's life within t~13 in this box. c39's longer re-issue (20261026T1042-c39-crawlers-noise-long-claim) is the place to test M.
